newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia bond yields cut again on budget hopes.
newsitem.headline: Australia bond yields cut again on budget hopes.

text.p: *Long-dated Australian bond yields eased to their lowest level since late February as the market continued Monday's rally in anticipation of a friendly budget next Tuesday.
Long-dated Australian bond yields eased to their lowest level since late February as the market continued Monday's rally in anticipation of a friendly budget next Tuesday, traders said.
The benchmark 10-year bond yield slipped to around 7.70 percent, easing some 15 basis points from last Thursday's post-wages data peak.
"The budget has been in the wings for sometime, but it's only the last few days that the market has begun to focus on it," one trader said.

Although this year's 1997/98 budget could prove to be a more low-key affair after the government's aggressive 1996/97 debut last year, there is some speculation that it could bring the underlying budget into balance a year earlier then projected.
There is also talk of a further reduction in new bond supply, with some analysts discussing the possibility of zero fixed-rate issuance.

The short end is also attracting a bid tone on the slimmest possibility of there being a further easing in monetary policy after today's Reserve Bank board meeting, although the general feeling is that official rates are on hold for some time.

Last week's strong wages report was seen making the chances of an easing less likely, and outweighing stubbornly currently high unemployment, the low inflation outlook and the patchiness of the economic recovery.
The market gets the latest on the labour force market on Thursday, and while a strong rebound in employment is expected, unemployment is expected to remain at 8.7 percent.
At the same time, RBA governor Ian Macfarlane is due to face a parliamentary finance committee on Thursday in the first of his semi-annual appearences, similar to U.S. Humphrey-Hawkins.

The local market outperformed the U.S., which succumbed to a subdued session ahead the two-leg refunding auctions. However, domestic bonds were outpaced by New Zealand, which released data showing higher than expected unemployment at 6.4 percent in the March quarter and a 0.1 percent fall in employment.
